steps.content: You walk in the sports field in the Bureau. The Sinners are free to move about in the designated area during this time of day, and today is no exception.
The afternoon sun is bright and warm. You look over to the bench by the fence and find Pacassi there as expected.
Pacassi budges up without closing the book in her hand.
What are you reading?

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: The History of the DisCity, 6th edition.
You have heard of it, a well-known historiographical work that has been reprinted many times.
What made you want to read this?

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: I want to know about the history of the DisCity.

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: But more than that, I want to know how you guys view the world...
So what do you think of the Bureau now?

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: It's great here. I don't have to be in all sorts of experiments and can even have time to myself.

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: I'm really happy with my life now.
She never goes out of control, always finishes the work given to her, and never makes any mistakes, even in battles, which isn't her strong suit... Pacassi has always been reassuringly stable.
But she also hardly interacts with others. She's always alone, like an outsider.
This isn't what you want to see.
Pacassi, I have some questions for you.

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: Aren't we going to the interrogation room?
No, you've already proven yourself.
Instead of as a Chief and a Sinner, I hope we can talk as friends.
Pacassi looks at you, her head slightly tilted, and closes her book.

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: What would you like to ask?
Pacassi takes the directory from you readily.
It's just some personal questions I have. I want to know more about Mayek.
I want to know about you guys' past.
Pacassi caresses the leather cover gently.

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: Mayek was once a prosperous city, with an ice-free port which was rare in the north, and an independent nuclear power plant.

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: Mayek had a population of half a million at its peak.

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: But that was all before Nightfall.
Pacassi flips through the directory. Each page was filled with names that were then crossed out.

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: Actually, for the first few decades, there wasn't a significant decline in the population of Mayek, thanks to the nuclear power plant.

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: But since thirty years ago, the town's population had dropped below ten thousand.
Five hundred thousand to ten thousand... What happened?

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: Thirty years ago, the nuclear power plant stopped running for the first time.

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: I had read Longyear's notes. It was just a problem with the cooling tower's pipes, but they couldn't figure it out at that time no matter how much they tried.

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: To prevent the reactor core from overheating, possibly causing an irreversible accident, they shut it down.

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: When the power plant was up and running again, the town had lost three thousand people.
Did they leave the town? Or...

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: It was December. No one could leave alive.

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: People thought they were merely stuck in the winter, which they could survive through with the nuclear power plant.

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: But it wasn't until that day did they realize that the winter was longer than they expected.
The warm sunlight pours on the pages, making the names in bright red particularly glaring.

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: Since then, the nuclear power plant had more and more frequent accidents, which could last from half a day to as long as a month.

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: Longyear was elected as the new mayor, because he fixed the cooling tower in the first accident. But what he couldn't fix was the distress in the residents' hearts.

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: People had enough of living in fear, enough of mashed potatoes with ice shreds. They heard about the DisCity in the south, far more prosperous than the town they were in.
Pacassi heaves a soft breath.

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: This kind of emotion reached its peak when I was four.
What happened?

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: Same as every time. Power outage.

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: A major power outage, lasting from summer to early winter.
Pacassi flips a few pages in the directory and points to a name.

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: Leroy was a great chef. Everyone loved his borscht. Even I still remember the taste of it.

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: He left Mayek that year. And there has been no restaurant in town ever since.
Pacassi continues to flip to the back of the directory.

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: Nastia was an elementary school teacher. Her daughter went missing the year before.

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: She searched for her daughter all winter.
Did she find her?

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: Yes.

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: At the end of summer, she found her under melted snow.

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: The three-month power outage forced everyone to plan for the worst.

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: That was when my parents left me.
Why didn't they take you with them?
Pacassi shakes her head.

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: I don't remember.

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: All I remember is that Longyear took me to his house later.

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: He gave me a place to live and made me fruit soup. Longyear told me he would fix the power plant, and everything would be fine.

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: But that year, when he was fixing the power plant, he lost his legs and his only son...

options: That must have been really tough for him
I'm the boss of the company, and I have to work my fingers to the bone to put food on the table. It's so demeaning...

choices.text: That must have been really tough for him
I'm the boss of the company, and I have to work my fingers to the bone to put food on the table. It's so demeaning...

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: Yes.

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: Perhaps...

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: But, at least he didn't abandon me, like he never abandoned Mayek.
What happened then?

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: After that, I took over his son's work, and became his assistant.

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: On top of the assigned work, I also helped him with chores and maintenance reports for the power plant.
What happened to the nuclear power plant after that?
Pacassi lowers her head.

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: Accidents happened more and more frequently, and there were fewer and fewer people in the town.

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: In the last two years, the power plant never started again. The remaining residents survived by demolishing abandoned houses for fuel.

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: And Longyear's mental health became more and more... unstable.

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: Everyone realized that perhaps all is lost for Mayek.
But you stayed till the end.

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: We later saw a glimpse of hope.
Pacassi lifts her head and looks at you.

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: One day, an oddly-dressed traveling merchant came to town.

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: He said he was from the DisCity and offered us a type of stone for sale—a stone that he claimed to provide protection from natural disasters.
Hypercubes?

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: Yes.

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: I bought the Hypercubes and the complementary device with spare precious metals in the nuclear power plant, and kept it secret from Longyear.

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: After we started up the device, we were able to repair the power plant in only two days. For the next two months, the plant ran stably.

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: Until Longyear found out about it...
What did he do?

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: He smashed the device, called us all traitors, and told us to get out.

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: At that time, there were only a dozen people or so left in the town.
Why did he do that?

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: Maybe he was just too tired... Or maybe he realized what he had been insisting for the whole time was totally pointless...

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: No one understood him. Everyone said he was out of his mind. He destroyed our last hope, and everyone left that summer.
So, in the last days, it was just you and Longyear?
Pacassi shakes her head.

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: In the last days, Longyear wouldn't talk to me. For the whole summer, he just wandered around the town without uttering a word.

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: Eventually, we were the only two left in the town. He showed up at my door and said to me,

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: "Why are you still here? Have you no shame? Get the hell out! Out of my town!"

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: I left Mayek... I abandoned him.

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: At that time, I just headed south with my mind totally blank.

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: It was only in the next evening when it started snowing that I realized I couldn't leave Longyear there alone.

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: When I raced back to the town, I found the power plant running, with thick steam rising from the cooling tower.

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: It was as warm as summer around the power plant, so warm, even the snow melted.

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: I searched everywhere. In the end I found Longyear asleep in the duty room in his wheelchair...
That was when the power plant...

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: I don't remember the details of what happened afterwards.

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: I just remember something rushing into my body and I didn't feel cold anymore.

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: When I woke up again, I was already in the DisCity.

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: Longyear, the nuclear plant, Mayek... they were all gone. I'm the only one that survived.
Longyear belonged there. He couldn't leave his past behind, but at the end of his life, he didn't want you to be buried with the past.
He protected you, Pacassi, even when he kicked you out of the town. He wanted you to find your future.

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: ...I don't need a future.

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: Everyone was leaving for the future, leaving the past behind.

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: No one remembered Mayek and Longyear.

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: Who else will remember them if I don't?

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: I don't want this to happen.
Ring—Ring—
A rapid bell rings, indicating that the free time for the Sinners is over.
Pacassi hands the directory back to you, picks up the book on the side, and stands up.

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: Thank you. Thank you so much for all you've done.

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: You are so kind. You listened to my dull stories, gave me books I wanted to read, and treated all Sinners equally... But I'm not like them... I don't belong here.

steps.speaker: Pacassi
steps.content: I should go now.
Pacassi heads toward the nearby building hurriedly. The afternoon sun shines on her face.
Yet you can't feel the slightest warmth.
